Today you learned two new angles: the {{< vocab "straight angle" zh=true >}} and the {{< vocab "full angle" zh=true >}}. Show a family member your turning angle and teach them the names!

## 1. Sort the angles

Write **acute**, **right**, **obtuse** or **straight** under each angle.

::: {.picture-answers cols="4" height="30mm"}
- ![](images/ws-g.svg) 1 | straight
- ![](images/ws-h.svg) 2 | right
- ![](images/ws-i.svg) 3 | obtuse
- ![](images/ws-j.svg) 4 | acute
:::

## 2. True or false?

Write **T** (true) or **F** (false).

::: true-false
- A straight angle is just a line. It is not an angle. | F
- Longer sides make an angle bigger. | F
- An obtuse angle is smaller than a straight angle. | T
- 1 full angle = 4 right angles. | T
- At 6:00, the clock hands make a straight angle. | T
:::

## 3. How far does it turn?

The {{< vocab "minute hand" zh=true >}} starts at 12. What angle has it turned?

**a.** after 15 minutes: {{< blank 4cm answer="a right angle" >}}  **b.** after 30 minutes: {{< blank 4cm answer="a straight angle" >}}

**c.** after 60 minutes: {{< blank 4cm answer="a full angle" >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 5. Challenge

**a.** How many right angles make 3 straight angles? {{< blank 1.5cm answer="6" >}}

**b.** Turn one side of a right angle until it makes a straight angle. How many more right angles did it turn? {{< blank 1.5cm answer="1" >}}

::: recall
- Tom says: "At 12:00 the clock hands make no angle." Lily says: "From 12:00 to 1:00, the minute hand turns a full angle." Who is right? Explain. | Both: at 12:00 the hands are together; in one hour the minute hand turns all the way round.
:::

## 6. Get ready for the next lesson

Next time we measure angles with a {{< vocab "protractor" zh=true >}}, in {{< vocab "degree" text="degrees" zh=true >}} (°). A right angle is **90°**. Can you guess?

**a.** A straight angle = 2 right angles = {{< blank 1.5cm answer="180" >}} °  **b.** A full angle = 4 right angles = {{< blank 1.5cm answer="360" >}} °
